newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Jiang vows Beijing to respect HK rights.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang vows Beijing to respect HK rights.

text.p: China's President Jiang Zemin pledged on Sunday to respect Hong Kong's rights and freedoms after the British territory reverts to Beijing sovereignty at midnight on Monday.
"We will firmly uphold the principles of 'one country, two systems' and 'Hong Kong people governing Hong Kong' as well as a high-degree of autonomy," the Xinhua news agency quoted Jiang as saying.

"We will... safeguard the Hong Kong residents' rights and freedoms in accordance with the law," Jiang said in a speech during a ceremony in Beijing's Great Hall of the People before setting off on the first leg of his journey to recover Hong Kong for China.

Jiang, who is also head of the Communist Party and commander-in-chief of the armed forces, will lead China's delegation to the handover ceremonies in Hong Kong at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday and is expected to cross the border into the British territory late on Monday.

His departure speech underlined Beijing's repeated pledges that it would uphold the "one country, two systems" formula created by late paramount Deng Xiaoping and under which Hong Kong retains its capitalist systems unchanged for 50 years.

China has been at pains to voice its determination to maintain Hong Kong's stability in the run-up to the handover, both to demonstrate that Beijing keeps its word and to win the trust of the people of rival Taiwan for reunification.

"Our delegation's trip to Hong Kong will surely reflect the feeling of glory and pride of all our nationalities regarding Hong Kong's return to the motherland and... reflects that our diplomatic manner is neither haughty nor humble," Jiang said.
"(Our delegation) will successfully fulfil our lofty mission to Hong Kong without fail," Jiang said.

Jiang, who is accompanied in the delegation by Zhuo Lin, widow of his late mentor Deng Xiaoping, and one of her daughters, pledged China would ensure the continued prosperity of the booming territory on its southern coast.
"This major move... demonstrates our resolute confidence to maintain the long-term prosperity and stability of Hong Kong," he said of the decision to send such a high-level delegation.
Beijing would take charge of Hong Kong's defence and foreign affairs but would "never interfere" in its domestic affairs. Foreign business and investment would be protected, he said.
"We will explain these principal policies to our people and the rest of the world," Jiang said.

After crossing the border and within hours of the entry of 509 People's Liberation Army troops, Jiang and Premier Li Peng are expected to sail across Victoria Harbour to Hong Kong island to receive the territory back from Britain's Prince Charles.

Jiang and the delegation, which includes Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, were expected to spend the night in the booming border town of Shenzhen, a creation of Deng's daring economic reforms, before crossing into Hong Kong.

Jiang would attend the swearing-in of Hong Kong's new Beijing-blessed legislature just after the handover ceremony in the early hours of Tuesday before returning to Beijing for huge celebrations planned in the Chinese capital.
